chunks: 4192 - And in the narration of Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, he said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the slaughter of a boy and a woman: may it be eaten? He said: “If the woman is Muslim and mentions the name of Allah over her slaughter, her slaughter is permissible. And the boy, if he is strong enough for slaughter and mentions the name of Allah, Exalted is He, his slaughter is permissible. That is when there is fear of losing the slaughtered animal and no one other than those two is found to slaughter.”

key_terms.حَلَّتْ: became lawful or permissible to eat
key_terms.خِيفَ فَوْتُ ٱلذَّبِيحَةِ: there is fear that the animal will be lost if not slaughtered promptly
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةِ: the slaughtered animal or the act of ritual slaughter in this legal context
key_terms.مُسْلِمَةً: a Muslim woman, indicating the condition of Islam for permissibility
key_terms.ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ: the name of Allah, whose mention is required over the slaughter
key_terms.ٱلْغُلَامِ: a young boy, here referring to one not yet fully mature but able to slaughter
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: a woman, whose slaughter is discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is the slaughter of a Muslim woman or a young boy permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the permissibility of slaughter performed by a Muslim woman or a capable boy. It states that their slaughter is lawful when the name of Allah is mentioned, specifically in a situation where the animal may be lost and no one else is available to perform the slaughter.
